newsitem.title: USA: Mich. Treasurer advancing $3.6 bln bond sale plan.
newsitem.headline: Mich. Treasurer advancing $3.6 bln bond sale plan.

text.p: The Michigan Treasurer's office hopes to introduce legislation creating an authority to sell $3.6 billion of school pension bonds before lawmakers adjourn for the summer next month, the director of legal and legislative affairs said Monday.

The treasurer has already selected a financial adviser, bond counsels and a syndicate of 23 underwriters to handle the massive deal, which must be completed by the end of the year to give employees the option of using a pension or defined contribution retirement plan, David White said.

The proposed legislation would create a public school employees finance authority to sell approximately $3.6 billion of taxable pension bonds to fully fund the school employees retirement system, White said.

Bond counsels and underwriters for the deal are still reviewing drafts of the proposed legislation and it could be introduced shortly after lawmakers return to Lansing in the fall if it is not ready in July, White said.
Treasurer Doug Roberts first disclosed in January that he was considering issuing taxable debt to fully fund the state's school employees retirement fund.
Roberts has said he would walk away from the deal if the state cannot get a better interest rate than eight percent.

White noted that under a state law, the retirement plan must be fully funded by the end of 1997 for the treasurer's office to offer employees the option of participating in the pension plan or choosing a defined contribution program.

The treasurer's office selected underwriters for the proposed funding shortly after announcing the selection of BancAmerica Securities Inc as financial adviser in April, White noted. Michigan used a request for proposal process to select the underwriters, he added.
Goldman, Sachs & Co and Smith Barney Inc have been selected as co-book running senior managers for the deal. Bear, Stearns & Co and J.P. Morgan Securities Inc have been chose as co-senior managers.
Third tier co-managers for the planned deal are Lehman Brothers, Morgan Stanley & Co Inc, PaineWebber/Salomon Brothers and Siebert, Brandford & Shank.

Fourth tier co-managers are Artemis Capital Group Inc, EVEREN Securities Inc, Graicap Inc, Tucker Anthony Inc, W.R. Lazard, Laidlaw Inc, Comerica Securities, First Chicago NBD Corp, M.R. Beal & Co, Robert W. Baird & Co Inc, First of America Securities, A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc, First of Michigan Corp, Merrill Lynch & Co, Southwestern Capital Markets Inc and Union Bank of Switzerland.
